extracted.intended_audience: journalists, members of the public, stakeholders in the enforcement action (e.g., healthcare providers, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: An official state (Attorney General) press release announcing a government enforcement settlement with a private company; includes headline, dateline, contact info, factual summary, quotes, legal context, and links to documents and reporting resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear headline stating parties, action, and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline: 'Attorney General Bonta, U.S. DOJ, Secure $18.2 Million Settlement with CVS, Resolving Allegations the Pharmacy Giant Submitted False Claims to Medi-Cal' — states the principal actors, the monetary amount, and the subject of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a concise headline that names the agency(ies), the defendant, the monetary figure (if appropriate), and the nature of the action. Avoid vagueness; include the most newsworthy elements. Anti-patterns: vague headlines without amount, missing defendant name, or headlines that bury the central fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Dateline: 'OAKLAND —' positioned before the body copy and date listed above the release (Monday, November 17, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear dateline (city) and an exact date so reporters and readers know where and when the announcement is issued. Use standard dateline formatting and place it at the start of the body. Omitting location/date reduces credibility and utility for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for media
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact: (916) 210-6000, agpressoffice@doj.ca.gov placed at top of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear media contact (phone and email) so journalists can follow up. Place contact info prominently near the top. Anti-pattern: no contact or only generic inboxes; outdated contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede paragraph summarizing the who/what/when/where/why
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening paragraph summarizes: 'California Attorney General Rob Bonta, in collaboration with the United States Department of Justice, announced a settlement with national pharmacy chain CVS Pharmacy, Inc. (CVS) over its alleged violations of the California False Claims Act... The settlement agreement requires CVS to pay $18.2 million.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First paragraph should concisely answer the key questions — who took action, against whom, for what, and the outcome (e.g., settlement amount). Keep it factual and focused. Avoid burying the main point several paragraphs in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific factual detail about allegations and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed allegation language: 'between 2010 and 2021, CVS submitted pharmacy claims to Medi-Cal using false electronic certifications... CVS knowingly failed to verify or document mandatory compliance for a large number of claims, resulting in the payment of millions of dollars of false claims by Medi-Cal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific factual contours: the alleged conduct, the time period, the program affected, and the mechanism (e.g., false electronic certifications). These specifics help reporters understand the scope and context. Avoid vague or legalistic descriptions without concrete details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative quote explaining significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote from official: 'Today’s settlement holds CVS accountable for its fraudulent drug dispensing and billing practices,' said Attorney General Bonta. Additional quote emphasizes responsibilities and program integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one quote from a named official that explains why the action matters and frames the agency's perspective. Quotes should be pithy, topical, and provide a human/authority voice. Anti-pattern: no quotes or quotes that restate facts without context or perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis and whistleblower context
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains legal mechanism and whistleblower role: 'The allegations resolved by this settlement were raised under the whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act... The whistleblower... alleged that CVS, motivated to quickly obtain claim payments, recklessly submitted billing codes without doing the necessary verification and documentation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the statute or legal authority underpinning the action and note if the matter originated from a whistleblower or referral. This increases transparency and helps readers understand procedural posture. Avoid omitting the legal basis when it is central to the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination and allocation of proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes collaboration and distribution: 'The settlement is the result of a joint effort by the California Department of Justice's Division of Medi-Cal Fraud and Elder Abuse (DMFEA) and the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California. ... the United States will receive 44.34% of the settlement proceeds.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple jurisdictions are involved, state the cooperating agencies and how proceeds or responsibilities are allocated. Provide percentages or figures when available to clarify federal/state splits. Anti-pattern: failing to attribute which agency led or how funds are distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to source documents and reporting resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides links: 'A copy of the settlement can be found here.' and referral link for reporting fraud at 'oag.ca.gov/dmfea/reporting'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include links to the underlying settlement, complaint, or reporting forms so interested parties can access primary documents. Also provide reporting or tip URLs. Broken or missing links reduce transparency and utility for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautionary/legal posture language
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains disclaimer: 'The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When announcing settlements or allegations, include a clear statement that allegations are not a determination of guilt or liability if applicable. This protects against misinterpretation and potential defamation concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational background and program context
rubrics_metrics.description: Background about enforcement division and funding: 'DMFEA protects Californians by investigating and prosecuting those who defraud the Medi-Cal program as well as those who commit elder abuse... The Division of Medi-Cal Fraud and Elder Abuse receives 75 percent of its funding from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services...' including FY 2026 funding figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise background on the enforcing office/division and relevant programmatic or funding context if it helps explain capacity, scope, or why the agency brought the action. Avoid long, unrelated organizational histories in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate and accessibility/translation notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Site boilerplate and translation disclaimer: Google Translate notice at top and general Office information/links are present; the release ends with 'State of California Department of Justice Office of the Attorney General' and site navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude with standard boilerplate about the agency and any necessary accessibility or translation disclaimers. Provide clear instructions for non-English speakers if translation tools are offered and disclaim accuracy. Anti-pattern: lacking translation/accessibility info when needed.
